# QS-CFW-1476-90 - Quality specification - connecting rod CFW-1476-90 (1045)
Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-1476-90

## Scope
This quality specification applies to the forging, heat treat verification, machining acceptance, and final inspection of connecting rod CFW-1476-90 (CFW-1476-90) produced at Plant P3. It defines mandatory acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for delivered parts and in-process lots. This document covers dimensional control of the rod bore, material hardness confirmation, and verification that the forging weight does not exceed the permitted maximum.

Background: The connecting rod is manufactured from 1045 material and processed through standard forging and heat treatment flows controlled by Plant P3 process instructions. Tight control of bore geometry and core hardness is required to meet service durability and press-fit assembly requirements. Controlling forging mass prevents die overloading and ensures thermal and metallurgical consistency.

Rationale: The specified acceptance limits were determined from design requirements and field service data to balance fatigue life, assembly clearance, and manufacturability. The bore tolerance ensures reliable fitment to mating components. The hardness band controls core strength without inducing excessive brittleness. The maximum forging weight protects tooling and process stability.

## Requirements table
| Characteristic | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Part identification | CFW-1476-90 |
| Hardness (core, post-heat-treat) | The hardness range for connecting rod CFW-1476-90 (CFW-1476-90) is 35-39 HRC. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for connecting rod CFW-1476-90 (CFW-1476-90) is ±0.03 mm. |
| Forging mass limit | The maximum forging weight for connecting rod CFW-1476-90 (CFW-1476-90) is 48.9 kg. |
| Traceability | Each lot must be retained with process route and inspection records in the quality record system for review. |

Notes on table entries: All acceptance decisions are based on measured values compared directly to the listed requirements. Where multiple bores are present on a single rod, each bore must meet the bore diameter tolerance entry. Hardness measurements must represent core condition after the final heat treatment process and prior to any final machining that alters microstructure. Forging mass is to be verified upon removal from the press and before heat treatment to confirm tooling and process stability.

## Inspection method
Visual and dimensional inspection is to be performed in a controlled inspection area following the plant inspection procedures. Use calibrated instruments appropriate to the measurement; calibration records must be current and available with the inspection records.

Hardness verification: Hardness shall be verified on a representative surface that reflects core material condition after heat treatment. Use a Rockwell hardness tester calibrated for the relevant scale. Verify indenter condition and machine calibration prior to testing. Record raw hardness readings and the averaged value for each sample in the inspection record. Compare the averaged value directly to the hardness requirement: The hardness range for connecting rod CFW-1476-90 (CFW-1476-90) is 35-39 HRC.

Bore diameter verification: Bore diameter inspection shall be performed using bore gauges or coordinate measurement equipment that deliver resolution sufficient to demonstrate compliance with the stated tolerance. Measurement technique must avoid deformation of the bore during verification. For bores that require gauging, use feeler and gauge methods that preserve surface finish. Record each bore measurement and identify the seated condition. Compare recorded bore diameters to the requirement: The bore diameter tolerance for connecting rod CFW-1476-90 (CFW-1476-90) is ±0.03 mm.

Forging mass verification: Verify forging mass on a calibrated mass measurement device capable of accepting the part. Measure each forging prior to heat treatment to confirm it does not exceed the mass limit. Record the measured mass adjacent to the lot identifier in the inspection record. Compare directly to the specified limit: The maximum forging weight for connecting rod CFW-1476-90 (CFW-1476-90) is 48.9 kg.

Sampling rationale: Sampling shall represent the production variation and process risk for the lot. Inspectors should select parts from across the lot to capture potential process drift. For lots exhibiting low variation in upstream process records, reduced verification density may be applied on an agreed basis between quality and production, with records documenting the rationale.

Examples:
- If hardness readings cluster narrowly within the range, record the individual results and mark the lot as accepted. If any reading falls outside the range, proceed to nonconformance handling.
- If a bore diameter measurement exceeds the ±0.03 mm tolerance in any dimension relative to nominal, mark the part nonconforming and follow containment steps.

Records to keep:
- Hardness test logs including raw readings, tester calibration certificate reference, operator initials, and part identifiers.
- Bore measurement logs including gauge identifiers, measurement method note, raw measurements, and operator initials.
- Forging mass log showing measured mass, scale calibration certificate reference, and part identifier.
- Lot route card showing processing steps, heat treat parameters reference, and operator acknowledgements.
- Nonconformance reports and disposition documents when applicable.

All records must be entered into the quality record system and linked to the lot or serial identifier for the product.

## Nonconformance handling
Containment: Any part that fails to meet the hardness, bore diameter tolerance, or forging mass requirement must be segregated immediately and clearly labeled as nonconforming. Notify quality engineering and production leadership to initiate investigation.

Disposition options: Quality engineering shall evaluate failed parts for potential rework or scrap. Rework possibilities include controlled machining when dimensional excess allows compliant restoration without violating material property requirements. Hardness failures shall not be corrected by localized heat input without prior approval from materials engineering. Forgings that exceed the maximum forging weight require process review and may be rejected for the lot if tooling or process correction is necessary.

Root cause and corrective action: Perform root cause analysis for any nonconformance that is systemic or repeated. Document findings, corrective actions, and verification steps in the nonconformance report. Apply process controls and operator training as required to prevent recurrence.

Example nonconformance workflow:
- Segregate affected parts.
- Record failure on nonconformance form and attach inspection records that show the deviation.
- Perform detailed review to determine whether rework is feasible without compromising part integrity.
- Implement corrective action and monitor subsequent lots to verify effectiveness.

Escalation: For any out-of-spec condition that could impact safety or field performance, escalate immediately to the plant quality manager for disposition and notification to stakeholders.

Record retention: Maintain all associated records in the quality record system as required by Plant P3 record retention practice. Records shall include inspection data, calibration references, nonconformance reports, and disposition paperwork to provide full traceability for the life of the product.

End of document.
